x.hook: Shared pool debt models are broken for farmers. Isolated margin on Soroban fixes this.
x.copy:
When you loop yield on Blend, you take on systemic liquidation risk from every other collateral asset in that pool.

Vanna isolates this. We route credit through dedicated SmartAccount sandboxes into Blend b-tokens. You get execution backed by ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, fixed 0.00014 XLM gas, and a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor. If a position fails, bad debt stays locked inside that individual account.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

linkedin.hook: Why pooled margin lending creates systemic risk in DeFi money markets
linkedin.copy:
Pooled liquidity protocols often expose depositors to tail-risk events across unrelated collateral assets. When a cross-margin system supports volatile long-tail collateral, a sudden cascade can leave the entire pool underwater. Blend v2 addresses this structural problem by isolating assets, and Vanna builds directly on this foundation by formalizing debt routing into yield-bearing b-tokens without cross-account contagion.

The architecture separates credit origination from pool-wide collateral baskets. By deploying isolated SmartAccount contracts on Soroban, leverage remains ring-fenced to individual positions. Risk engines monitor solvency with a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor, relying on ~320ms Mercury indexer latency to process position state changes before underwater trades threaten the protocol core. Transaction execution remains predictable with a fixed 0.00014 XLM gas profile per state mutation.

The result is clean institutional credit infrastructure for Stellar. Lenders retain sovereign counterparty risk isolation while farmers capture native yield without sharing default risk with arbitrary borrowers. Builders can spin up testnet instances to verify the b-token routing logic directly at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: How we route margin credit into Blend v2 b-tokens without shared pool contagion on Soroban
reddit.copy:
Most DeFi lending protocols still rely on shared-pool debt accounting. If one user deposits an illiquid asset, borrows against it, and gets liquidated during high volatility, bad debt bleeds into the common pool. Depositors take a haircut for risks they never priced.

When designing Vanna on Soroban, our goal was to eliminate this contagion while allowing farmers to scale credit into Blend v2 b-tokens.

### Architectural Overview

Instead of holding user positions in a single monolithic contract, Vanna provisions isolated SmartAccount instances for each borrower. When you open a margin position:

1. Capital routes into the user-owned SmartAccount sandbox.
2. The contract executes deposits directly into Blend v2, receiving b-tokens as collateral.
3. The position maintains an enforced 1.10x Health Factor floor.

Because the contract logic is formally verified and sandboxed, bad debt cannot escape the SmartAccount boundary. Lenders supply capital to the core vault, but individual position risks remain strictly segregated.

### Performance and Monitoring

Cross-contract calls on Soroban are cheap enough to make granular position management practical. State updates run at a fixed 0.00014 XLM gas fee. Off-chain liquidation bots monitor position health using Mercury indexers, which feed state updates with ~320ms latency. This low latency makes it possible to maintain narrow liquidation spreads without prematurely liquidating active positions during temporary spread blowouts on Stellar DEX pairs.

### Testing It Out

We have open-sourced the interface for testnet deployments. You can spin up an isolated SmartAccount sandbox, mint mock liquidity, and route margin into Blend test pools.

Head over to test.stellar.vanna.finance to connect your wallet and deploy a test contract.

Feedback on the b-token redemption paths and gas consumption is welcome.

*Disclosure: I am a core contributor building Vanna Protocol on Stellar.*
